implementation_notes: Swift's `Codable` synthesis is the scatter generator: a struct's coding keys, its `init(from:)`, its `MemberwiseInitializer` call sites and its SwiftUI previews all change when a field is added, and previews are easy to forget. The idiomatic consolidation is a single wire type plus a mapping to a domain type, so the synthesised `Codable` belongs to one struct only. SwiftUI previews are the canonical forgotten site — a preview that stops compiling is the cheapest possible detector, and leaving them out of the target is what makes the scatter invisible.
idiom_name: Codable struct field added to every view model and preview
pitfalls: Preview providers are the least-run code in a SwiftUI app and are the most common place a constructor change is missed.
Default values in memberwise initialisers let a new field be omitted silently at call sites that use them.
Property wrappers (`@State`, `@Environment`) mean the 'where does this field get set' question has several answers.
